thread.title: Report: Apple to slow hiring; Austin’s new mega-campus on track

author: ABJ staff
title: Report: Apple to slow hiring; Austin’s new mega-campus on track
text: By ABJ staff Jan 16, 2019, 11:15pm CST With iPhone sales falling short and revenue forecasts dragged down, Apple Inc. will cut back on hiring for some divisions, Bloomberg reports, citing anonymous sources. The intel was reportedly gathered after CEO Tim Cook met with employees earlier this month. In that meeting, Bloomberg reports, he said Austin is still on track to add a huge tentacle to its large Austin campus — and an expansion in Los Angeles was also specified as safe. Cook reportedly dropped the news to select employees a day after he authored a letter to investors about the company’s recent woes, particularly in China . During the meeting, Cook said he didn’t expect a hiring freeze — just that “some divisions would reduce hiring,” Bloomberg reports. Austin has a lot at stake. Not only are about 6,200 Apple employees already here, but the company announced in December that 5,000 more are on the way to a soon-to-be-built extension to the Austin campus. The investment is pegged at about $1 billion. The new 133-acre facility will be able to handle about 5,000 employees when it opens, and could grow to house up to 15,000 — more than Dell Technologies Inc. employs at its headquarters a few miles away. Dell’s (NYSE: DELL) Austin-area headcount is hovering around 12,000, down from previous years. Jobs at the expanded Apple campus will include engineering, research and development, operations, finance, sales and customer support. Even without them, Austin is already able to boast of having the most Apple employees outside the headquarters in Cupertino, Calif. Bloomberg reports that Cook hasn’t decided yet which divisions will need to pare down. Groups such as Apple’s artificial intelligence team will continue to add new employees at a strong pace, Bloomberg sources said. Apple shares (Nasdaq: AAPL) finished slightly up on Wednesday, ending the day at $154.94 but after-market activity was a bit more trepidatious. Track its performance in real time here . In related news, Apple's typical employee probably makes far less than you think: $55,426 per year. That's according to a Jan. 8 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. For comparison, the median employee at social media giant Facebook makes more than $240,000 per year. At Google parent Alphabet Inc., it's more than $197,000. By ABJ staff Jan 16, 2019, 11:15pm CST Related Content
